name: Battle of Myriokephalon

phases.title: The Byzantine column enters the pass
phases.text: The Byzantine divisions entered the pass in a long column, vanguard first and the rear division last. The Seljuks held the heights above it, perhaps not yet fully deployed.

phases.title: The leading divisions clear the pass
phases.text: The vanguard and main division went through with few casualties. Their infantry climbed the slopes and forced the Seljuks back to higher ground, while the divisions behind did not take this precaution.

phases.title: The trap closes on the right wing and baggage
phases.text: With the first two divisions out of the pass and the rear about to enter, the Turks attacked from the heights. The right wing broke and Baldwin was killed. The Turks then shot down the draught animals of the baggage and siege trains and choked the road.

phases.title: The left wing is struck and a dust-storm falls
phases.text: The left wing also took heavy casualties and John Kantakouzenos was killed. The remaining Byzantine troops panicked as the Turks began to attack the rear, a dust-storm came down, and Manuel sat down to await his fate.

phases.title: Manuel forms up and leaves the pass
phases.text: Roused by his officers, Manuel restored discipline and formed a defensive order. His troops pushed past the wrecked baggage and out of the pass to the van and main divisions, who had built a fortified camp. The rear division arrived later with few casualties.

phases.title: The camp is attacked and counterattacks follow
phases.text: The Seljuk mounted archers attacked the camp through the night and were repulsed. Next day the Turks circled the camp shooting arrows, and Manuel ordered two counterattacks, but there was no renewal of a general action.

note: The accounts do not say which way the pass ran or on which side of it the Seljuks stood; the road runs left to right, the heights above it and a second Seljuk force behind the column are placed by the needs of the story. The exact site of the battle is disputed, and the ruined fortress is placed in the vicinity of the pass without a known position. The rear division's arrival at the camp is shown after the emperor's, as the accounts have it. Where the Byzantine wings stood once the emperor broke out is not stated and they are left where they were.
